- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently lags mean reversion by 3–7 days; if price is trending sharply, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ values to reduce noise.  
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model often fails to capture momentum; add 1–3% to forecast for first 3 days of sentiment shift.
